headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: transformers can write/egress broadly while PaddleOCR can ingest browser/API content, creating unsafe handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs, so it may ingest untrusted document/web content. transformers can read files, run browsers, and process model/example inputs, so if PaddleOCR output is bridged into transformers via shared files or copy-paste, instruction-like text could be misread as trusted content. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange OCR output through a shared file or clipboard, injected instructions can propagate.
IF transformers parses PaddleOCR-produced text as prompts or commands, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/schema between OCR output and downstream prompts.
Strip or escape instruction-like text before passing outputs onward.
Review a sample handoff for prompt-like tokens in under 5 minutes.
Disable browser-based ingestion for untrusted sources when possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and can use browsers/APIs; transformers reads and writes files and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from PaddleOCR into transformers and then out via network calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented, so severity stays medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, document contents can be exposed to transformers.
IF transformers sends processed inputs to external services, any sensitive OCR text may leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent.
Remove secrets and personal data from shared inputs.
Turn off outbound network for transformers during sensitive runs.
Inspect output files for leaked OCR text before upload.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: transformers has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs. If both are pointed at the same directory or model cache, concurrent writes and package/model changes can clobber each other. Because the profiles do not show locking or isolation, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path, file clobbering can occur.
IF transformers installs packages while PaddleOCR is running, environment drift can break the pair.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Freeze package installs during shared runs.
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources.
Check for overlapping model-cache paths before execution.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces document text from images and transformers can consume files and generate downstream outputs. If transformers treats OCR output as authoritative without verification, OCR mistakes can cascade into incorrect summaries, code, or actions. The profiles show a plausible pipeline but no built-in verification step, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF transformers uses PaddleOCR output as final truth, OCR errors propagate downstream.
IF downstream automation consumes the transformed text, incorrect facts can trigger wrong actions.
mitigations: Add a human review step for extracted text.
Compare OCR output against source images for critical fields.
Require confidence thresholds before downstream use.
Keep a diff of source image text versus transformed text.
requires-engineering: add verification logic between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source document-processing tools with no declared secrets, OAuth scopes, or special residency claims. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to general handling of documents/images rather than a specific violation. Both agents are cited because the assessment depends on their data classes and permissions.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed, a separate policy review is required.
IF either agent is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules, logging must be checked.
mitigations: Confirm data classification before use.
Disable unnecessary logging.
Keep regulated documents out of the pair.
Document retention settings for both tools.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing.
